job_paths.title: Backend Developer (Python, Django)
job_paths.summary: Build, test, and deploy secure, performant RESTful APIs and backend services using Python, SQL, Django, and Django REST Framework.

capstone.title: Multi-tenant task management platform API
capstone.brief: Design, develop, optimize, secure, and test a complete multi-tenant Task Management REST API capable of serving real-world client applications.
milestones: Capstone planning: Define user stories, database ERD diagrams, and RESTful endpoint specifications.
Project endpoints: Implement CRUD resources for projects using DRF viewsets and serializers.
Task endpoints: Build nested task resources with status tracking and user assignment logic.
Ownership boundaries: Enforce strict multi-tenant authorization so users only access their organization's data.
API quality and UX: Standardize exception handling, custom validation error messages, and pagination structures.
Deployment readiness: Configure environment variables, CORS policies, security settings, and static collection.
Observability and maintenance: Integrate logging, API health check endpoints, and query execution timing metrics.
Capstone polish: Expand the APITestCase suite to achieve high coverage and fix discovered edge cases.
Demo and retrospective: Generate final OpenAPI documentation, complete README instructions, and present project architecture.

job_paths.title: Frontend Developer (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)
job_paths.summary: Build accessible, responsive, interactive web applications from scratch using standard web technologies and public APIs.

capstone.title: Interactive public API web application
capstone.brief: Design, build, and deploy a responsive, fully accessible single-page web application that fetches data from a public REST API, allows user filtering and sorting, and saves user preferences using localStorage.
milestones: Plan application wireframes, component structure, and select a CORS-enabled public API.
Construct the HTML foundation using semantic layout tags and accessible ARIA attributes.
Apply CSS grid and flexbox layouts to ensure mobile-first responsive styling.
Implement asynchronous Fetch API calls to retrieve data from the public endpoint with error handling.
Render fetched data dynamically in the DOM with interactive filtering, searching, and sorting controls.
Implement local storage persistence to save user preferences across page reloads.
Conduct keyboard navigation and accessibility checks to ensure compliance with WCAG standards.
Finalize code polish, test across different screen sizes, and publish the application.

job_paths.title: Full Stack Developer (JavaScript front end, Django back end)
job_paths.summary: Build, secure, and deploy complete web applications from scratch using standard HTML/CSS/JavaScript frontends and Python Django REST backends.

capstone.title: Custom full-stack web application with authentication
capstone.brief: Design, build, and deploy a full-stack web application based on your own original project concept, featuring a Django REST API backend, token authentication, and a responsive JavaScript frontend.
milestones: Project discovery and planning: Define user stories, REST API specifications, database ERD schema, and frontend UI wireframes.
Backend API setup: Implement Django models, REST serializers, and viewsets with token authentication endpoints.
Frontend interface: Build semantic HTML structure, responsive CSS layout, and interactive DOM components.
API Integration: Wire JavaScript fetch requests to Django API endpoints with full CRUD capabilities.
Authentication integration: Implement client-side user registration, sign-in, token storage, and protected session logic.
Error handling and UX polish: Standardize form validations, error notifications, loading indicators, and user feedback.
Deployment preparation: Configure production environment variables, database settings, WhiteNoise static file hosting, and CORS rules.
End-to-end testing and launch: Execute full-stack integration tests, deploy backend and frontend services, and publish final documentation.

skill_paths.title: Python basics
skill_paths.summary: Learn core Python programming concepts from basic data types and control structures to functions, error reading, and an introduction to classes.

courses.title: Python data types and control flow

chapters.title: Variables and primitive types
chapters.learning_goal: you can declare variables and perform arithmetic and boolean operations with integers, floats, and booleans
chapters.exercise_idea: Define price, quantity, and tax variables, then calculate the total bill amount as a float.

chapters.title: Strings and string formatting
chapters.learning_goal: you can manipulate text using string methods, slicing, and f-string interpolation
chapters.exercise_idea: Clean messy user name inputs with strip and title methods, then output a formatted welcome message.

chapters.title: Lists and dictionaries
chapters.learning_goal: you can store, retrieve, update, and remove elements in Python lists and key-value dictionaries
chapters.exercise_idea: Create a dictionary representing a user profile, append new entries to its 'roles' list, and retrieve specific key values.

chapters.title: Conditions and logic
chapters.learning_goal: you can write conditional execution blocks using if, elif, else, and logical operators
chapters.exercise_idea: Write an authorization check that verifies if a user is active and possesses admin privileges before granting access.

chapters.title: Loops and iteration
chapters.learning_goal: you can iterate over sequences and collections using for and while loops
chapters.exercise_idea: Loop through a list of transaction amounts, calculate the total sum, and count transactions exceeding 100.

chapters.title: Functions and parameters
chapters.learning_goal: you can write reusable functions with positional arguments, default parameters, and return values
chapters.exercise_idea: Write a function that calculates discounted item prices based on user role with a default 0% discount.

chapters.title: Modules and imports
chapters.learning_goal: you can import functions, constants, and modules from the Python standard library
chapters.exercise_idea: Import the datetime and random modules to generate randomized order IDs and timestamp current dates.

chapters.title: Reading errors and exceptions
chapters.learning_goal: you can interpret Python error tracebacks and handle exceptions gracefully using try-except blocks
chapters.exercise_idea: Wrap unsafe dictionary key lookups and numerical divisions in try-except blocks to return fallback default values.

chapters.title: First look at classes
chapters.learning_goal: you can define basic classes with __init__ constructors, instance attributes, and custom methods
chapters.exercise_idea: Create a User class storing username and email attributes with a method that returns a formatted profile tag.

project.title: Command-line inventory manager
project.brief: Build a modular Python script that manages product inventory data using custom classes, dictionary lookup tables, functions, and exception handling.

placement_test.title: Python Basics Placement Test
placement_test.summary: Verify student readiness for Django Foundations by evaluating core Python knowledge across all 9 prerequisite chapters.
placement_test.pass_mark: 8 out of 10 multiple-choice questions correct AND both short coding tasks fully passing (minimum 80% overall score).

multiple_choice_questions.question: Which data type is produced by the division operation `10 / 2` in Python?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Standard division `/` in Python always evaluates to a float type.

multiple_choice_questions.question: What is the output of `'  hello '.strip().upper()`?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: `.strip()` removes leading and trailing whitespace, and `.upper()` converts the string to uppercase.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Given `user = {'name': 'Alex', 'role': 'admin'}`, how do you access the value `'admin'`?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Dictionary values are retrieved using square brackets with the corresponding key string.

multiple_choice_questions.question: What does the expression `not (5 > 3 and 2 == 4)` evaluate to in Python?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: `5 > 3` is True and `2 == 4` is False, making the `and` expression False. `not False` evaluates to True.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How many iterations will `for i in range(2, 6):` perform?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: `range(2, 6)` produces values 2, 3, 4, and 5, resulting in exactly 4 iterations.

multiple_choice_questions.question: What value is returned by a Python function that does not contain an explicit `return` statement?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Python functions implicitly return `None` when no explicit `return` expression is executed.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Which import statement allows calling `sqrt(16)` directly without using a module prefix?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: `from module import function` brings the function directly into the local namespace.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Which exception is raised when attempting to access a key that does not exist in a Python dictionary?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Accessing a missing key on a dictionary raises a `KeyError`.

multiple_choice_questions.question: In a Python class method definition, what does the first parameter (conventionally named `self`) represent?
options: The specific instance of the class
multiple_choice_questions.correct_option: The specific instance of the class
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: `self` refers to the instance upon which the method was invoked.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Which list method adds a new item to the end of an existing list in place?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: `.append(item)` modifies the list in place by adding the given item to the end.

coding_tasks.prompt: Write a function `filter_products(products, max_price)` that accepts a list of product dictionaries `[{'name': str, 'price': float}]` and a maximum price float. Return a list containing only the names of products whose price is less than or equal to `max_price`.
coding_tasks.test_case_idea: Pass `[{'name': 'Widget', 'price': 10.0}, {'name': 'Gadget', 'price': 25.0}]` with `max_price=15.0` and assert returned list is `['Widget']`.

coding_tasks.prompt: Define a `BankAccount` class with an `__init__` constructor accepting `owner` (str) and an optional initial `balance` (float, default 0.0). Add a `deposit(amount)` method that adds to balance, and a `withdraw(amount)` method that subtracts from balance or raises a `ValueError('Insufficient funds')` if `amount > balance`.
coding_tasks.test_case_idea: Instantiate `account = BankAccount('Alice', 100.0)`, call `account.deposit(50.0)` (balance 150.0), and verify that `account.withdraw(200.0)` raises `ValueError`.

skill_paths.title: JavaScript programming fundamentals
skill_paths.summary: Master JavaScript fundamentals, control structures, functional programming, and data manipulation.

chapters.title: Variables, data types, and operators
chapters.learning_goal: you can declare variables and perform operations using primitive JavaScript data types
chapters.exercise_idea: Declare let and const variables, check types with typeof, and perform arithmetic and string concatenation.

chapters.title: Control flow and loops
chapters.learning_goal: you can implement conditional logic and loops to control program execution
chapters.exercise_idea: Write if/else conditional blocks and for loops to evaluate numerical thresholds and repeat operations.

chapters.title: Functions and scope
chapters.learning_goal: you can write reusable functions using parameter passing, return statements, and arrow syntax
chapters.exercise_idea: Refactor repeated calculation code into modular arrow functions with explicit return values.

chapters.title: Working with arrays
chapters.learning_goal: you can manipulate JavaScript arrays using push, pop, shift, unshift, and slice
chapters.exercise_idea: Write functions to add, remove, and extract specific elements from an array of strings.

chapters.title: Higher-order array methods
chapters.learning_goal: you can iterate and transform data using map, filter, reduce, and forEach
chapters.exercise_idea: Filter an array of item objects by price and map the results to a list of title strings.

chapters.title: Objects and JSON
chapters.learning_goal: you can store and access structured data using JavaScript objects and JSON syntax
chapters.exercise_idea: Parse a JSON string into an object, modify property values, and serialize it back to JSON.

project.title: Interactive quiz engine
project.brief: Build a JavaScript logic module that parses question data objects, scores user selections, and returns formatted feedback.

skill_paths.title: Git and GitHub
skill_paths.summary: Master version control fundamentals and collaborative GitHub workflows for team software development.

chapters.title: Git repository fundamentals
chapters.learning_goal: you can initialize a Git repository and check repository status
chapters.exercise_idea: Initialize a local repo, create a .gitignore file, and verify untracked files using git status tests.

chapters.title: Commits and staging
chapters.learning_goal: you can stage modified files and commit changes with clear log messages
chapters.exercise_idea: Stage specific files using git add and write a formatted commit message verified by test assertions.

chapters.title: Branching and merging
chapters.learning_goal: you can create git branches, switch context, and merge feature branches into main
chapters.exercise_idea: Create a feature branch, commit a change, switch back to main, and perform a fast-forward merge.

chapters.title: Remote repositories and pushing
chapters.learning_goal: you can link local repositories to remotes and push local branches
chapters.exercise_idea: Configure a remote origin URL and push commits to a simulated remote repository.

chapters.title: Pull requests and code reviews
chapters.learning_goal: you can construct pull request descriptions and inspect diffs
chapters.exercise_idea: Parse a Git diff patch and generate structured markdown pull request documentation.

chapters.title: Resolving merge conflicts
chapters.learning_goal: you can identify, resolve, and finalize Git merge conflicts
chapters.exercise_idea: Inspect conflicting markers in a file, resolve the conflict manually, and finalize the merge commit.

project.title: Collaborative Git workflow
project.brief: Initialize a Git repository, create feature branches, resolve a merge conflict, and prepare a clean pull request.

skill_paths.title: SQL basics
skill_paths.summary: Query, filter, join, and manage relational database schemas using standard SQL queries.

chapters.title: Selecting and filtering data
chapters.learning_goal: you can write SELECT statements with WHERE conditions to query database records
chapters.exercise_idea: Write SQL queries to retrieve specific user fields filtered by active status and date range.

chapters.title: Sorting and aggregating results
chapters.learning_goal: you can aggregate data using GROUP BY and sort results with ORDER BY
chapters.exercise_idea: Calculate total order counts per customer grouped by user ID and ordered by highest total.

chapters.title: Joining relational tables
chapters.learning_goal: you can combine data across related database tables using INNER and LEFT JOINs
chapters.exercise_idea: Write a query joining user profiles and orders to display customer names alongside order status.

chapters.title: Inserting, updating, and deleting data
chapters.learning_goal: you can modify database rows using INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE queries
chapters.exercise_idea: Execute INSERT statements for new products and UPDATE price fields based on condition rules.

chapters.title: Table creation and data constraints
chapters.learning_goal: you can construct database tables using CREATE TABLE with constraints
chapters.exercise_idea: Create a tasks table with PRIMARY KEY, NOT NULL, and UNIQUE column constraints.

chapters.title: Foreign keys and indexing
chapters.learning_goal: you can enforce referential integrity with foreign keys and create indexes
chapters.exercise_idea: Define foreign key references between tasks and projects tables and index the author_id column.

project.title: Relational database design and querying
project.brief: Design a multi-table database schema with foreign keys, populate sample data, and write complex JOIN queries.

skill_paths.title: Django foundations
skill_paths.summary: Build structured web applications with Django models, migrations, administration views, and user relationships.

courses.title: Core Python web and Django architecture

chapters.title: Python and HTTP foundations
chapters.learning_goal: you can parse HTTP request methods, headers, and status codes in Python
chapters.exercise_idea: Write a Python script to parse HTTP request strings and build structured HTTP response dictionaries.

chapters.title: Django project anatomy
chapters.learning_goal: you can configure Django project settings, manage apps, and route URL patterns
chapters.exercise_idea: Configure INSTALLED_APPS and map root URL patterns to simple HTTP view functions.

chapters.title: Models and migrations
chapters.learning_goal: you can define Django model fields and execute migration commands
chapters.exercise_idea: Define a Project model with string, boolean, and datetime fields, then generate migration files.

chapters.title: Django admin
chapters.learning_goal: you can customize the Django admin interface for model management
chapters.exercise_idea: Register custom models in admin.py with list_display, list_filter, and search_fields settings.

chapters.title: Users and ownership
chapters.learning_goal: you can associate Django models with the User model to enforce resource ownership
chapters.exercise_idea: Add a ForeignKey pointing to settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL and auto-assign request.user on save.

chapters.title: REST and serializers
chapters.learning_goal: you can convert Django models into JSON representations using serializers
chapters.exercise_idea: Implement a Django REST Framework ModelSerializer with field validations.

chapters.title: Testing fundamentals
chapters.learning_goal: you can write automated unit tests for Django models and API views
chapters.exercise_idea: Write TestCase classes testing model creation, custom methods, and HTTP response codes.

project.title: Core task manager application
project.brief: Create a Django core app featuring user-owned Task models, migration files, custom Django admin setup, and unit tests.

skill_paths.title: Django REST Framework
skill_paths.summary: Develop production-grade REST APIs complete with viewsets, authentication, filtering, and OpenAPI docs.

chapters.title: Viewsets and routers
chapters.learning_goal: you can construct DRF ModelViewSets and register automated URL routers
chapters.exercise_idea: Define a ModelViewSet for projects and wire it to a DefaultRouter instance.

chapters.title: Authentication and permissions
chapters.learning_goal: you can secure REST endpoints using Token authentication and object-level permissions
chapters.exercise_idea: Implement custom BasePermission classes ensuring users can only modify their own resources.

chapters.title: CRUD design
chapters.learning_goal: you can design clean RESTful CRUD endpoints following HTTP standard practices
chapters.exercise_idea: Override viewset perform_create and perform_update hooks to attach metadata to objects.

chapters.title: Filtering and search
chapters.learning_goal: you can enable searching and backend field filtering on DRF viewsets
chapters.exercise_idea: Configure DjangoFilterBackend and SearchFilter with specific filterset_fields.

chapters.title: Pagination and ordering
chapters.learning_goal: you can configure API response pagination and field ordering rules
chapters.exercise_idea: Implement a custom PageNumberPagination class and OrderingFilter on list endpoints.

chapters.title: Validation and errors
chapters.learning_goal: you can write custom serializer validations and format error payloads
chapters.exercise_idea: Add field-level and object-level validate() methods raising standardized ValidationError exceptions.

chapters.title: API documentation
chapters.learning_goal: you can generate OpenAPI schemas and interactive documentation for APIs
chapters.exercise_idea: Annotate DRF views using drf-spectacular schema decorators to publish API documentation.

project.title: Secured and documented REST API
project.brief: Build a feature-complete RESTful API with token authentication, custom permissions, query filtering, pagination, and OpenAPI docs.

skill_paths.title: Advanced Django backend development
skill_paths.summary: Optimize database queries, handle safe transactions, organize app architecture, and write integration tests.

chapters.title: Database relationships
chapters.learning_goal: you can design relational Django models using OneToOne, ForeignKey, and ManyToMany fields
chapters.exercise_idea: Model project member roles using ManyToManyField with an explicit through table.

chapters.title: Querysets and performance
chapters.learning_goal: you can optimize database queries using select_related and prefetch_related
chapters.exercise_idea: Refactor a viewset queryset using select_related and prefetch_related to eliminate N+1 queries.

chapters.title: Transactions and safety
chapters.learning_goal: you can protect data updates using atomic database transactions
chapters.exercise_idea: Wrap multi-table updates inside transaction.atomic() blocks to ensure rollbacks on errors.

chapters.title: Reusable app structure
chapters.learning_goal: you can decouple features into independent, modular Django app modules
chapters.exercise_idea: Extract user profile logic into an isolated, reusable application package.

chapters.title: Settings and environment variables
chapters.learning_goal: you can manage environment variables and isolate development/production settings
chapters.exercise_idea: Configure django-environ to read secret keys and database URLs from environment files.

chapters.title: Security essentials
chapters.learning_goal: you can configure Django security headers, CORS settings, and rate limiting
chapters.exercise_idea: Configure SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT, CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, and throttle rate limits.

chapters.title: Integration testing
chapters.learning_goal: you can write end-to-end integration tests using DRF APITestCase
chapters.exercise_idea: Write APITestCase test flows covering multi-step user authentication, task creation, and authorization failure.

project.title: Optimized and secured backend architecture
project.brief: Refactor a Django project for high query efficiency, atomic transactions, decoupled environment configurations, and integration test coverage.

skill_paths.title: HTML and CSS foundations
skill_paths.summary: Structure and style modern, responsive, and accessible web pages using semantic HTML and CSS.

chapters.title: Document structure and semantic tags
chapters.learning_goal: you can structure web documents using semantic HTML5 tags like header, nav, main, article, and footer
chapters.exercise_idea: Replace generic div elements in an unstructured HTML document with appropriate semantic HTML5 layout tags.

chapters.title: Forms and input elements
chapters.learning_goal: you can create accessible HTML forms using labels, input types, and field validation attributes
chapters.exercise_idea: Build a user registration form containing text, email, password, select dropdowns, and required validation attributes.

chapters.title: Media and links
chapters.learning_goal: you can embed images, video, and hyperlinks with appropriate fallback attributes
chapters.exercise_idea: Add responsive image elements with descriptive alt attributes and external links opening safely in new tabs.

chapters.title: Box model and CSS positioning
chapters.learning_goal: you can manipulate box dimensions, padding, margins, borders, and positioning modes
chapters.exercise_idea: Adjust box-sizing, padding, and margins on card components to eliminate unwanted layout overflow.

chapters.title: Flexbox layouts
chapters.learning_goal: you can align and distribute page elements dynamically using CSS Flexbox
chapters.exercise_idea: Build a navigation bar and flex child items using justify-content, align-items, and flex-wrap properties.

chapters.title: CSS grid layouts
chapters.learning_goal: you can construct multi-column grid layouts using CSS Grid properties
chapters.exercise_idea: Design a photo gallery layout using grid-template-columns, gap, and fractional grid units.

chapters.title: Responsive web design and media queries
chapters.learning_goal: you can write media queries to adapt layouts across mobile, tablet, and desktop viewports
chapters.exercise_idea: Write breakpoint media queries that stack multi-column flex containers vertically on small screen viewports.

chapters.title: Accessible structure and ARIA attributes
chapters.learning_goal: you can enhance web accessibility using ARIA roles, labels, and landmarks
chapters.exercise_idea: Annotate interactive icon buttons and modal popups with aria-label and aria-expanded attributes.

chapters.title: Color contrast and visual accessibility
chapters.learning_goal: you can audit and adjust CSS color contrast ratios and focus indicators
chapters.exercise_idea: Modify low-contrast text colors and explicit focus ring outlines to meet WCAG AA standards.

chapters.title: Keyboard navigation and screen readers
chapters.learning_goal: you can make interactive elements fully navigable using keyboard tab order
chapters.exercise_idea: Fix tabIndex values and keyboard event handlers so custom buttons are fully focusable and triggerable via Enter and Space keys.

project.title: Responsive accessible personal portfolio page
project.brief: Build a fully responsive and keyboard-accessible personal portfolio website using semantic HTML5 and plain CSS.

skill_paths.title: Dynamic web development with JavaScript
skill_paths.summary: Connect HTML and CSS to JavaScript to create interactive, event-driven web apps that consume REST APIs.

chapters.title: Selecting and modifying DOM elements
chapters.learning_goal: you can query HTML elements and modify their content, styles, and attributes using JavaScript
chapters.exercise_idea: Use querySelector to select elements and update textContent, classList, and inline styles dynamically.

chapters.title: Event listeners and event propagation
chapters.learning_goal: you can handle user interactions using event listeners and event delegation
chapters.exercise_idea: Attach click and input event listeners to forms and list containers using event delegation.

chapters.title: Dynamic HTML rendering
chapters.learning_goal: you can dynamically create, append, and remove HTML elements in response to user input
chapters.exercise_idea: Build a dynamically updating to-do list where items can be created, marked completed, or deleted from the DOM.

chapters.title: Asynchronous execution and promises
chapters.learning_goal: you can manage asynchronous code using JavaScript Promises and setTimeout
chapters.exercise_idea: Create a function returning a Promise that resolves after a delay or rejects on error conditions.

chapters.title: Fetching data with Fetch API
chapters.learning_goal: you can make GET requests to external APIs using fetch and async/await
chapters.exercise_idea: Fetch a list of user profiles from a JSON API using async/await and render the output as HTML cards.

chapters.title: Error handling and loading states
chapters.learning_goal: you can handle API fetch errors and display loading states to the user
chapters.exercise_idea: Wrap fetch calls in try/catch blocks to display error messages on network failure and show spinner indicators during load.

project.title: Live weather dashboard application
project.brief: Develop a dynamic web dashboard that fetches weather data from a REST API, handles user search inputs, and renders current conditions.

skill_paths.title: Full-stack integration and deployment
skill_paths.summary: Connect vanilla JavaScript client interfaces to Django REST Framework APIs with token authentication and production deployment.

courses.title: Connecting front end to Django REST API

chapters.title: CORS and API cross-origin requests
chapters.learning_goal: you can configure Django CORS headers and issue cross-origin fetch requests from a JavaScript front end
chapters.exercise_idea: Configure django-cors-headers settings in Django and write frontend fetch calls to exchange JSON data across origins.

chapters.title: Full-stack CRUD operations
chapters.learning_goal: you can wire HTML form events and dynamic JavaScript DOM updates to Django REST viewsets
chapters.exercise_idea: Build a client dashboard that issues POST, PUT, and DELETE fetch requests to a Django API and updates DOM elements in real time.

chapters.title: Handling API state and UI feedback
chapters.learning_goal: you can render loading states, handle HTTP status codes, and present backend validation errors in the frontend UI
chapters.exercise_idea: Parse Django REST validation error response payloads in JavaScript and render inline error messages next to form inputs.

chapters.title: Token-based authentication integration
chapters.learning_goal: you can implement token login flows by storing authentication tokens in client storage and attaching authorization headers
chapters.exercise_idea: Write a login fetch handler that posts credentials to Django, saves the returned token in localStorage, and sets Authorization headers on subsequent requests.

chapters.title: Protected routes and user state
chapters.learning_goal: you can restrict client-side view navigation and conditional rendering based on authentication state
chapters.exercise_idea: Build a JavaScript route guard that redirects unauthenticated users to a sign-in view and displays personalized account data when logged in.

chapters.title: Session persistent logout and token refresh
chapters.learning_goal: you can handle token expiry, user logout, and session clearance in the frontend
chapters.exercise_idea: Implement a sign-out mechanism that deletes stored tokens from localStorage and resets the frontend user interface.

chapters.title: Production build configuration
chapters.learning_goal: you can prepare Django static file serving and frontend assets for production deployment
chapters.exercise_idea: Configure WhiteNoise and STATIC_ROOT settings in Django to serve compiled static frontend assets directly.

chapters.title: Environment management and cloud deployment
chapters.learning_goal: you can deploy Django APIs and static JavaScript frontends using environment variables on platform-as-a-service providers
chapters.exercise_idea: Set up production environment variables for database URLs, secret keys, and allowed hosts for cloud hosting.

chapters.title: Full-stack health monitoring and CORS security
chapters.learning_goal: you can verify end-to-end full-stack connectivity and secure production CORS origins
chapters.exercise_idea: Write a client-side health check diagnostic and restrict production CORS origins to match deployed client domains.

project.title: Integrated auth and task dashboard
project.brief: Connect a vanilla JavaScript frontend interface to a Django REST API, implementing full token authentication, CRUD operations, error handling, and production deployment settings.
